english: For a real number $\lambda$, let $f_\lambda:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f_\lambda(x)=2x^{3}+6x^{2}+\lambda x+27$. The set of all real numbers $\lambda$ for which the equation $f_\lambda(x)=0$ has exactly one real root is an interval of the form $(\alpha,\infty)$. Then the value of $\alpha$ is ______.
hindi: वास्तविक संख्या $\lambda$ के लिए, माना $f_\lambda:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f_\lambda(x)=2x^{3}+6x^{2}+\lambda x+27$ द्वारा परिभाषित है। उन सभी वास्तविक संख्याओं $\lambda$ का समुच्चय, जिनके लिए समीकरण $f_\lambda(x)=0$ का ठीक एक वास्तविक मूल है, $(\alpha,\infty)$ के रूप का एक अन्तराल है। तब $\alpha$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $\lambda\geq6$: $f_\lambda'\geq0$, $f_\lambda$ strictly increasing, hence one-one; with $f_\lambda(\pm\infty)=\pm\infty$ it has exactly one real root (IVT)
$\lambda<6$: $f_\lambda$ increases, decreases, increases (not one-one), with turning points $x_1<x_2$; exactly one root iff $f_\lambda(x_1)f_\lambda(x_2)>0$
The count changes only when a turning value is $0$, i.e. a double root: $f_\lambda=f_\lambda'=0$

$\lambda=0$: turning values $f(0)=27$, $f(-2)=35$, both positive, one root; so one root for all $\lambda>-31.5$; at $\lambda=-31.5$, $f=2\left(x-\dfrac32\right)^{2}(x+6)$ has two distinct roots, and for $\lambda<-31.5$ three
solution_full: If $\lambda\geq6$, then $f_\lambda'(x)\geq0$ with equality at most at $x=-1$, so $f_\lambda$ is strictly increasing on $\mathbb{R}$ and hence one-one. As $f_\lambda(x)\to-\infty$ when $x\to-\infty$ and $f_\lambda(x)\to\infty$ when $x\to\infty$, the intermediate value theorem gives a root, and one-one-ness makes it the only one.

If $\lambda<6$, $f_\lambda'$ has two zeros $x_1<x_2$; $f_\lambda$ increases on $(-\infty,x_1]$, decreases on $[x_1,x_2]$ and increases on $[x_2,\infty)$, so it is many-one. By Rolle's theorem two roots would need a zero of $f_\lambda'$ between them, so on each of the three monotonic pieces there is at most one root, and $f_\lambda=0$ has exactly one real root exactly when the local maximum $f_\lambda(x_1)$ and the local minimum $f_\lambda(x_2)$ have the same sign.
As $\lambda$ varies the number of real roots can change only when a turning value is $0$, i.e. when $f_\lambda$ has a double root $x$: $f_\lambda(x)=0$ and $f_\lambda'(x)=0$.

From $f_\lambda'(x)=0$: $\lambda=-6x^{2}-12x$. Substituting, $2x^{3}+6x^{2}-6x^{3}-12x^{2}+27=-4x^{3}-6x^{2}+27=0$, i.e. $4x^{3}+6x^{2}-27=0=(2x-3)(2x^{2}+6x+9)$. The quadratic factor has discriminant $36-72<0$, so $x=\dfrac32$ and $\lambda=-6\cdot\dfrac94-18=-\dfrac{63}{2}$.

So the root count is constant on $\left(-\dfrac{63}{2},\infty\right)$ and on $\left(-\infty,-\dfrac{63}{2}\right)$. At $\lambda=0$ the turning points are $x=0$ and $x=-2$ with $f_0(0)=27>0$ and $f_0(-2)=35>0$, so there is exactly one root; hence exactly one root for every $\lambda>-\dfrac{63}{2}$.

At $\lambda=-\dfrac{63}{2}$, $f_\lambda(x)=2\left(x-\dfrac32\right)^{2}(x+6)$ has two distinct real roots, and for $\lambda<-\dfrac{63}{2}$ (e.g. $\lambda=-40$: $f(-2)>0$, $f(2)=-5<0$) there are three.
Therefore the required set is $\left(-\dfrac{63}{2},\infty\right)$ and $\alpha=-31.5$ (the one-one condition alone would wrongly give $6$).
originality_note: New: the set of parameters giving exactly one real root is larger than the set where the cubic is one-one; the boundary comes from the double-root condition f = f' = 0, which factors through a cubic with a single rational root (way 5). Closest known: values of k for which x^3 - 3x + k = 0 has one/three real roots (k as a constant term). Different because: the parameter multiplies x, so the turning points move with lambda; the monotone case lambda >= 6 and the non-monotone case must be joined at the double-root value -63/2.
blueprint_concepts: One-one vs many-one: monotonicity, horizontal line and algebraic tests
Root Counting via Calculus: Combining Rolle’s theorem, IVT, and monotonicity to find exact number of real roots.

concept_use.One-one vs many-one: monotonicity, horiz: For lambda >= 6, f is strictly increasing and hence one-one, so it has at most one root; for lambda < 6 it is many-one.
concept_use.Intervals of monotonicity: f' = 6(x+1)^2 + lambda - 6 gives the intervals of increase and decrease and the turning points x1 < x2 for lambda < 6.
concept_use.Root Counting via Calculus: Combining Ro: IVT gives at least one root; Rolle limits each monotonic piece to one root; the root count changes only at the double-root value lambda = -63/2, found from f = f' = 0.

stem_review: Read as a student: the family, the equation and the phrase 'exactly one real root' are clear; the boundary lambda = -31.5 gives two distinct roots, so the set is open at alpha; for lambda = 6 the root is simple (2(x+1)^3 + 25), so no multiplicity question arises; verified with sympy (discriminant zero only at -63/2 among reals) and numerically for lambda in {-40, -31.6, -31.5, -31.4, -20, 0, 6, 50}; matches the plan 'negative decimal'. Changed: No change.
key_step: Join the monotone case (lambda >= 6) with the turning-value sign test; the boundary is the double-root value from f = f' = 0, lambda = -63/2.
justification: Two ideas linked: monotonicity/one-one-ness for one root and the double-root condition for the change in the number of roots; the natural trap (answering 6) and the cubic for the tangency point make it a genuine Advanced-average question, numerical. Comparable to 2023-P2-Q7 (L3) on counting fixed points through convexity and monotonicity, and above 2024-P2-Q10 (L1) where monotonicity alone settles the count.
